intro.say: A push moves something away from you. A pull moves it towards you. Let's try!

rounds.say: When you push a shopping cart, it rolls away from you. That's a push!
rounds.caption: Push = away from you

rounds.say: When you pull a sled by its rope, it comes towards you. That's a pull!
rounds.caption: Pull = towards you

rounds.ask: Kicking a ball. Is it a push or a pull?

options.label: Pull
options.why: Your foot sends the ball away, so it's a push.

rounds.explain: Your foot pushes the ball away from you.

rounds.ask: Pulling a carrot out of the ground. Push or pull?

options.label: Push
options.why: The carrot comes towards you, so it's a pull.

rounds.explain: You bring the carrot towards you, so it's a pull.
Pushes send things away. Pulls bring things closer.

options.label: Push a cart
options.why: The cart moves away from you, so that's a push.

options.label: Kick a ball
options.why: Kicking sends the ball away, so that's a push.

rounds.explain: Reeling brings the fish towards you, so it's a pull.

options.label: Pull up socks
options.why: Socks come up towards you, so that's a pull.

options.label: Pick a carrot
options.why: The carrot comes towards you, so that's a pull.

rounds.explain: Your fingers push the keys down.

intro.say: Pushes and pulls are called forces. Forces make things start, stop and turn!

rounds.say: A ball sits still. Kick it, and it starts to move. A push made it start!
rounds.caption: Forces start things

rounds.say: A goalkeeper catches the flying ball, and it stops. A force can stop things too.
rounds.caption: Forces stop things

rounds.say: Hit a moving ball with a bat, and it flies off another way. Forces can turn things.
rounds.caption: Forces turn things

rounds.ask: A goalkeeper catches the ball. What does the force do?

options.label: Starts it
options.why: The ball was already moving. The catch stops it.

options.label: Turns it
options.why: The ball doesn't go another way. It stops.

rounds.explain: Catching is a force that stops the ball.

rounds.ask: Which makes a toy car go faster?

options.label: Gentle push
options.why: A small push gives a small, slow start.

rounds.explain: A harder push gives more force, so the car goes faster.

rounds.ask: Which needs the biggest push to move?

options.label: Balloon
options.why: A balloon is very light. It needs only a tiny push.

options.label: Box
options.why: Something here is even heavier.

rounds.explain: Heavier things need a bigger push to move.

rounds.ask: Does the force start it or stop it?
rounds.explain: Some forces get things moving, and some forces stop them.

options.label: A colour
options.why: A force isn't a colour. It's a push or a pull.

options.label: A sound
options.why: A force isn't a sound. It's a push or a pull.

rounds.explain: Every push and every pull is a force.

intro.say: Let's solve tricky puzzles about pushing, pulling, and which way things go.

rounds.say: In tug of war, both teams pull. The team that pulls harder wins, and the rope moves their way.
rounds.caption: The stronger pull wins

rounds.say: Gravity is a pull too! It pulls everything down towards the ground. That's why a dropped apple falls.
rounds.caption: Gravity pulls down

rounds.ask: Tug of war! Three kids pull left and one kid pulls right. They are all just as strong. Which way does the rope go?

options.label: Right
options.why: Only one kid pulls that way. The other side pulls harder.

options.label: Nowhere
options.why: The pulls are not equal, so the rope moves.

rounds.explain: Three kids pull harder than one, so the rope moves left.

rounds.ask: You throw a ball up high. What pulls it back down?

options.label: Wind
options.why: Wind blows sideways. Something pulls everything down.

options.label: The Sun
options.why: The Sun doesn't pull the ball down to the ground.

rounds.explain: Gravity always pulls things down towards the ground.

rounds.ask: Two kids push a box from opposite sides, just as hard. What happens?

options.label: Moves left
options.why: The pushes are equal, so neither side wins.

options.label: Moves right
options.why: The pushes are equal, so neither side wins.

rounds.explain: Equal pushes balance each other, so the box doesn't move.

rounds.ask: A heavy box won't move. What could help?

options.label: Push gently
options.why: A gentler push is even weaker.

options.label: Whisper to it
options.why: Words can't move a box!

rounds.explain: Two people make a bigger force together.

rounds.ask: Order these from the smallest push needed to the biggest push needed.
rounds.explain: The heavier something is, the bigger the push it needs.

rounds.ask: What force moves a sailboat across the lake?

options.label: Fish pulling it
options.why: Fish don't pull boats! Look at the big sail.

options.label: Gravity lifting it
options.why: Gravity pulls down, not across.

rounds.explain: The wind pushes on the sail and the boat moves along.
